text:
You need a custom internal API that can hit GPU-backed processing, return MP3 files, and stay fast and scalable for your web and native clients.

I’m Tobias Reyne, and I’ve spent 7 years building full stack products with JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Node.js, PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, HTML, and CSS. While your API would be built in Python, I’m very comfortable designing the product-side architecture and the data flow around performance-sensitive backend services, and I’ve worked on internal systems where reliability, permissions, and speed mattered.

One relevant project was a staff onboarding portal for healthcare staffing. I built an internal React and NestJS portal with PostgreSQL, TypeORM, and Auth0 where nurses uploaded credentials and managers approved them, with permissions per region. It supported 2,400 staff and reduced onboarding paperwork from 5 days to 1 day.

Another relevant project was embedded customer analytics for a B2B SaaS product. I built usage dashboards in React and TypeScript with Node.js and PostgreSQL so each customer account could see its own metrics. It rolled out to 140 customer accounts and was delivered 3 weeks early.

For your API, I’d focus on a clean request/response design, careful handling of long-running GPU work, and performance-conscious integration with the consuming apps. Since this is internal only, we can optimize for practical throughput, predictable behavior, and a simple interface for your web and native clients. I’d also pay close attention to how MP3 generation requests are queued, processed, and returned so the system stays as fast as possible under load.

If helpful, I can think through the API shape, latency risks, and scale considerations with you before implementation. What does the GPU workflow look like today, and do you already know whether the MP3 generation needs to be synchronous or can be handled asynchronously with polling or callbacks?
